resolution: Settled by printed text, read literally: Pure ignores "all other attributes", and the Manual names Tough as an attribute ("4. Attributes like Tough"), so Tough, Balanced, Inverted and Unaware do not apply in a Pure interaction. The owner ruling of 2026-08-20 (“{Pure}: the attribute layer, switched off…”)’s "stats are not attributes" is our ruling and does not change what the Manual calls Tough. attr.general.pure states print; the engine keeps the stat attributes on: F-U19-1 (CT-260, filed as an owner decision on whether to change the engine). Document fix: done 2026-10-10. attr.pure.stat-attributes (which stated the owner ruling of 2026-09-05 (“{Pure} outside combat: the same switch…”)) and attr.pure.unaware-combat (which stated the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“STAT LAYER 6, {Unaware}: everything in…”)) contradicted attr.general.pure; both now state print and are marked engine-differs (F-U19-1, F-U19-2). Register fix: mark the owner ruling of 2026-09-05 (“{Pure} outside combat: the same switch…”)’s "still read" sentence and the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“STAT LAYER 6, {Unaware}: everything in…”)’s "survives {Pure}" as outranked by the printed reminder.

resolution: Question for the owner. The rule follows the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”), which the owner ruled on 2026-08-22 with both worked examples in view (the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”) addendum quotes _passer in full). The _passer posts are in #rules-questions, not a [Solved] RAQ write-up, so they do not outrank the owner. If the owner chooses B, the engine change is one line in effStats (79-round17-layers.test.ts names it).

question.ask: Does Inverted invert from the printed stats, or from a rewritten base?

readings.label: A
readings.text: From the rewritten base: a base rewrite is a new base, not a stat change (the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”); spikeydog).
readings.table: A 10/15 made base 4/4 with a +1/+1 counter, Inverted, is a 3/3.

readings.label: B
readings.text: From the printed stats: any difference from the printed stats is a stat change (the owner ruling of 2026-08-25 (“the owner's answers to the 27…”); _passer's two posts).
readings.table: The same unit, Inverted, is a 15/25.

question.follows: A (owner ruling of 2026-08-23, “Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”), the owner's ruling of 2026-08-22.
question.recommend: B, for one definition of a stat change: the owner's later general words (owner ruling of 2026-08-25, “the owner's answers to the 27…”) and _passer agree, and Unaware already reads a base rewrite as a change. Keep A only if the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”) was meant as a deliberate exception for Inverted.

summary: Whether a unit without Flying may block a Flying column together with a Flying unit in the same blocking column. The printed reminder names units; the Manual says "the blocking unit"; the Rulebook says "unless the defending player also has flying units"; the owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“the reminder a player reads is…”) records that the client "blocks by COLUMN".

sides.quote: Only flying units can block flying units.
blocked unless the blocking unit has flying.
Flying attribute and the entire column cannot be blocked unless the defending player
blocks by COLUMN and the authored row said so.
Its column can only be blocked by a column with Flying.

resolution: Question for the owner. No test plays the shared case and no designer source addresses it: the printed reminder names units, the Manual "the blocking unit", and the Rulebook "the defending player".

question.ask: May a unit without Flying block a Flying column together with a Flying unit in the same blocking column?

readings.label: A
readings.text: Yes: attributes are shared in a column in all situations, so the non-Flying unit has Flying and the column may block.
readings.table: A Flying blocker lets its column-mate join the block.

readings.label: B
readings.text: No: every unit that blocks a Flying column must have Flying itself.
readings.table: A non-Flying unit may never stand in a column blocking Flying.

question.follows: Neither: the rule states only the restriction both readings share. Our glossary row and the owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“the reminder a player reads is…”) ("blocks by COLUMN") describe A.
question.recommend: A: Caleb says column-mates share attributes "in all situations" (owner ruling of 2026-08-23, “Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”), and A is the permissive reading.

resolution: Follow the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“a document validated against the code…”): an Unaware card can be targeted, and stat changes put on it do nothing while it is Unaware. Mark the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“STAT LAYER 6, {Unaware}: everything in…”)’s targeting paragraph "(answered by the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“a document validated against the code…”))". summary: The Tough + Inverted law rests on the owner's retracted bug report and the owner ruling of 2026-08-28 (“{Tough} + {Inverted}: the owner's own…”)’s derivation; the owner's own words ("always kills") are stronger than the law the owner ruling of 2026-08-28 (“{Tough} + {Inverted}: the owner's own…”) pins (a shrunk unit survives).

sides.quote: > works. So tough + inverted always kills the unit since +0/+X is just -0/-X
> ### **final defense = −2Δ.** The base cancels out completely.

resolution: Follow the owner ruling of 2026-08-28 (“{Tough} + {Inverted}: the owner's own…”): the rule states the law (defense = -2 x the net change), which is the owner's statement for every board where the defense has not been reduced. No designer source; Caleb's nearby remark ("tough inverted would die before you could add more", the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”)) agrees with the common case.
